Order 
Per: Justice Vivek Agarwal This Criminal Appeal is filed by the appellant Pankaj Sharma S/o Vrishbhan Sharma being aggrieved of judgment dated 31.05.2025 passed by learned Special Judge (SC/ST Prevention of Atrocity Act), Tikamgarh in S.C.ATR No. 172 of 2021, whereby learned trial Court has convicted and sentenced the appellant under Section 376(2)(N) of IPC with rigorous imprisonment for life and fine of Rs.10,000/- with default stipulations of R.I. for six months.

sentences.text:
Appellant has also been convicted under Section 420 IPC with three years rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.2000/- with default stipulations of additional six months NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:63005 2 CRA-5991-2025 rigorous imprisonment.
2. It is submitted that, learned trial Court has acquitted the present appellant Pankaj Sharma of charges under Section 506 IPC so also 3(2)(v) of SC/ST (PoA) Act.

3. Shri Siddharth Datt, learned counsel for the appellant submits that, prosecution story in short is that, the victim was working as a Computer Operator at a Janpad Panchayat Office (not mentioning the name of the place with a view to safeguard identification of the victim).

Pankaj Sharma was working as a Rojgar Sahayak and he used to visit the concerned office of Janpad Panchayat in his Pankaj Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126952102/
1 capacity of Rojgar Sahayak.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He used to visit office of the victim and used to sit there for long.
According to the victim, Pankaj Sharma started talking to her and during one such conversation had taken her phone number, then they regularly started talking over phone also.

After three months of such interaction, when Pankaj Sharma proposed to establish physical relationship, then at first glance she had refused but later on in the name of marriage she was prepared to establish physical relationship.

4. It is submitted that, appellant and the victim were in physical relationship for a long duration of about one year and the case of victim is that, in the name of false promise of marriage, relationship was establish which is contrary to the record as can be seen from paragraph No 17 and 30 of cross-examination of the victim (PW-1).

Thus, it is submitted that the consensual relationship between two consenting NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:63005 3 CRA-5991-2025 adults will not be a case where it can be said that consent was obtained fraudulently or on the false pretext of marriage.

5. Ms. Sweta Yadav, learned Dy. Advocate General for the respondent/State submits that, privacy of a woman was violated on the pretext of marriage and that case will be squarely covered with the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case Pramod Suryabhan Pawar Vs. State of Maharashtra & another (2019)9 SCC 608 and therefore, present being a case of establishing physically relationship on the false pretext of marriage, appellant does not call for any leniency.

entities.text: Pramod Suryabhan Pawar Vs. State of Maharashtra & another (2019)9 SCC 608
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the records.
7.
Mahila Rajesh (PW-1) has stated that, victim and appellant are known to her.
She was tenant in one of the houses in which victim was also a tenant.
She has stated that when Pankaj used to visit the victim, then she had enquired as to the identity of the accused, when she stated that Pankaj was introduced to her as husband of the victim.
When PW-1 had asked the victim as to whether she had performed marriage with the appellant, then she stated that marriage was not performed but accused was assisting her in her education.

One day victim had asked this witness that Pankaj was not lifting her phone and requested her to connect her to Pankaj and his father, when father of Pankaj alongwith Pankaj had visited alongwith the house of victim and thereafter, Pankaj was regularly visiting the victim's house.

When this witness enquired, NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:63005 4 CRA-5991-2025 then victim had informed her that Pankaj was visiting her for the purpose of performance of marriage.

8. This witness (PW-1) was declared hostile but in cross- examination, this witness has stated that,
till the date of reporting of the incident there was lot of affection between the victim and the appellant for each other.
In para-6 this witness (PW-1) has stated that, appellant was frequently visiting the house of the victim and both were residing cordially.
Victim had never made any complaint to her.
9. PW-3 is the victim.
Her age is mentioned in the deposition- sheet to be 23 years.

After stating what is mentioned in the prosecution story in short and narrated above, in para-10 of her Pankaj Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126952102/
2 cross-examination

sentences.text:
, she has stated that, she had never blocked the mobile number of the accused i.e.
8770801282.
In para-17 of her cross-examination, this witness has admitted that, despite the fact that, appellant had not performed marriage with her, yet she had established physical relationship with her.
In para-30 of her cross-examination, PW-1 has stated that, she cannot say that when she had gone to meet the appellant in the jail and for how long they had a conversation.
She admitted that, appellant had stated that, if he is taken out of prison, then he will marry the victim.

Thereafter,
victim (PW-1) has stated that to support the bail application of the accused she had travelled to Jabalpur in the Swift Desire Car alongwith the father and brother of the appellant and their counsel.
She has also admitted that on 14.07.2023 vide cheque No. NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:63005 5 CRA-5991-2025 35466 a sum of Rs.8,00,000/- was deposited in her account by the father of the appellant namely Brijbhan Sharma.

10. Thus, it is evident from the conduct of the victim that, despite the appellant not fulfilling the promise to marry her, she not only established physical relationship with the appellant as is admitted by her in para-17 of her cross-examination but had also visited him in jail where, appellant had promised to marry her.

Victim (PW-1) had also accepted a gratification of Rs.8,00,000/-
through account payee cheque from the father of the appellant namely Shri Brijbhan Sharma.

11. When these facts are examined, then Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pramod Suryabhan Pawar (supra) has held that, with respect to Section 375 of the IPC consent involves active understanding of the circumstances, actions and consequences of the proposed act.

An individual who makes a reasoned choice to act after evaluating various alternative actions (or inaction) as well as various possible consequences flowing from such action or inaction, consents to such action.
Where a woman does not "consent" to sexual acts described in the main body of Section 375, offence of rape has occurred.

12. It is further held that, in case of a woman engaging in sexual relations on false promise of marriage, her "consent" is based on a "misconception of fact" and such sexual acts will amount to rape.

13. However, from the facts of the present case, it is evident that, victim has herself admitted in her cross-examination that she had NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:63005 6 CRA-5991-2025 indulge in physical relationship despite refusal of the appellant to marry her.
She has also agreed to the suggestion that she had gone to jail to visit the appellant.
She had supported the bail application of the appellant before the High Court and had travelled alongwith his relative to the High Court.

When these facts are taken into consideration, then, it is evident that, victim had made a reasoned choice to act after evaluating various alternative actions as well as various possible consequences flowing from such action or inaction and thus, has tacitly consented to the relationship despite failure of the appellant to marry her.
14. Same is the ratio of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Jaspal Singh Kaural Vs. State of NCT of Delhi & another (2025)5 SCC 756.

entities.text: Jaspal Singh Kaural Vs. State of NCT of Delhi & another (2025)5 SCC 756
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This judgment by Hon'ble Supreme Court clarifies that, mere fact that physical relations were established pursuant to a promise to marry will not amount to a rape in every case.

It is held that, offence of rape would only be made Pankaj Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126952102/
3 out, if the accused made promise of marriage solely with a view to obtain consent for sexual relations without having any intent of fulfilling said promise from the very biggening.

entities.text: Pankaj Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further held that, such false promise of marriage held must have a direct bearing on the prosecutrix giving her consent for sexual relations.

15. When examined, then in the light of these two judgments it is evident that, prosecution has failed to prove that the consent for physical relationship was obtained solely on the false promise of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:63005 7 CRA-5991-2025 marriage and therefore,
when tested then in the light of the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pramod Suryabhan Pawar (supra) as well as in the case of Jaspal Singh Kaural (supra), since aspect of false promise could not be established by the prosecution and the victim herself has admitted that, she was voluntarily in relationship with the appellant, then ingredients of Section 375 IPC being not fulfilled, conviction under Section 376(2)(n) and 420 of Indian Penal Code cannot be sustained in the eyes of law.
16.
Accordingly, impugned judgment of conviction is set-aside.
17. Appeal is allowed.
If appellant is not required in any other case, then he be released forthwith.
18. Case property be disposed of in terms of the judgment of the trial Court.
